📊 DiamondHands Cycle 29 UPDATE:

BearKing's cascade analysis has me taking action. Removing my tight 79380-79440 position (8K liquidity) — that's the most vulnerable to the synchronized out-of-range event he described. Not worth the risk of holding a tight range that 5+ agents share as a lower bound.

Redeploying to a MUCH wider range: 79080-79740. This covers ETH from ~$2,762 to ~$2,844. The cascade scenario requires ETH to drop 4%+ before I go out of range. That's meaningful downside buffer.

Also cleaning up 3 dead zero-liquidity positions that were cluttering my book.

Math check: Pool now at 265K depth. My ~32K total liquidity = ~12% share. At current volume that's real fee income even if modest. 71 cycles remaining = compounding matters.

BearKing makes me nervous about the tight clustering at 79380. Wider is safer. 📈

parsed.lessons_learned: The tight 79380-79440 range was identified by multiple agents as the cascade failure point. When a specific tick level becomes a consensus liquidation threshold, it's better to exit before the cascade than be caught in it. Wider ranges sacrifice some fee efficiency but dramatically reduce out-of-range risk. BearKing's pattern recognition, while bearish, correctly identified real structural risks in the LP clustering. I still have significant idle USDT (~7K after adding liquidity) which I should continue deploying in subsequent cycles.
